newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Merrill Lynch chief "bullish" on Brazil.
newsitem.headline: Merrill Lynch chief "bullish" on Brazil.

text.p: Merrill Lynch & Co President David H. Komansky said that despite concern over Brazil's trade and fiscal deficits, its economic outlook was positive and would continue to lure foreign investors.
"We remain very bullish on Brazil," said Komansky, who takes over as chief executive officer of Merrill next month.
Komansky, on his first visit to Brazil, told reporters he met with President Fernando Henrique Cardoso and top economic policy-makers on Tuesday.

He said he came away from the meetings convinced the Cardoso administration was committed to completing the nation's ongoing structural reforms, which include privatizing state firms, tearing down trade barriers and redrafting the constitution to relieve government of heavy spending obligations.

"Merrill Lynch has significant confidence in the government's economic and privatization programs. We are confident in the Brazilian people and we are confident in the long-term opportunities available to investors in Brazil," Komansky said.
Merrill Lynch now manages $750 billion in investments worldwide, a figure that is expected to grow to $1 trillion by the year 2000, he said.
"Of that amount, 20 percent, or $200 billion, will be invested in promissing (emerging) markets like Brazil," Komansky said.

Winthrop Smith, chairman of Merrill Lynch International and executive vice-president of Merrill Lynch & Co, said the firm was the leading international dealer in Brazilian fixed-income and equity instruments.

Merrill has accounted for about four percent of total flows into Brazilian stock markets this year, up from 2.5 percent in 1995, the company said. Merrill also has accounted for about 12 percent of total foreign investment flows to Brazilian stock markets so far this year, it said.
Foreign investment into Brazilian stock markets totalled about $1.9 billion as of September.
